clue.text: Like an incompetent, in the main?

definitions.meaning: someone incompetent is floundering, unable to cope with a task beyond their ability
the main is the open sea, where a swimmer may find the water too deep to stand in

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone beyond their ability, and literally a swimmer in water too deep to stand.

clue.text: Soldier on duty — regular one about to board tender

parts.note: orderly means regular, methodical

indicators.note: to board is to get on, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to tender is to offer
the Roman numeral for one is I
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A methodical soldier is about to climb aboard a supply boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to board' puts IC inside OFFER.
explanation.definitionFit: An orderly officer is the officer detailed for the day's duties in a unit.

clue.text: Small piece of mosaic from the Durbeyfield period?

parts.note: Tess Durbeyfield is the heroine of Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A fragment of mosaic is dated to the era of Hardy's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Tess Durbeyfield is the heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles or cubes of stone or glass used to build up a mosaic.

clue.text: Cobweb, perhaps, in extremely filthy atmosphere

indicators.note: in places the atmosphere piece within the letters taken from filthy
extremely points to the extremes of the word filthy, its first and last letters

parts.note: air means atmosphere

explanation.surface: A spider's web hangs in a dirty, smoky room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes F and Y from 'filthy'; 'in' puts AIR between them. Cobweb is a fairy in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, not a spider's web.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobweb is one of Titania's fairy attendants in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so an example of the class.

clue.text: Leading band, say, is familiar with Wagner's operas

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word as spoken, keeping only its sound

parts.note: to be familiar with something is to know it, so knows
Wagner's Ring cycle is his set of four operas

explanation.surface: A top band claims to know Wagner's operas well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns KNOWS into its sound-alike NOSE. 'Leading' looks like 'top', but a nose ring is the band through a bull's nose by which it is led.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull is led by a ring through its nose, so the ring is literally a band used for leading.

clue.text: Old Turkish line judge in the Kent area?

indicators.note: in places the line and judge abbreviations within the regional letters

parts.note: Kent lies in the south-east of the United Kingdom, SE UK

explanation.surface: A line judge from Kent turns out to be of Turkish descent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the south-east corner of England, which is how 'the Kent area' gives its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seljuks were a Turkish dynasty ruling much of western Asia in the 11th to 13th centuries.

clue.text: Endlessly speed up printing unit brought in for shift

indicators.note: brought in means one piece is put inside the other
endlessly means the last letter is cut from the word for speed up

parts.note: to expedite is to speed up
an en is a unit of measure in printing

explanation.surface: A rushed print job needs an extra unit brought in for the shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' is a noun here, a makeshift means, not a work period.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean a means to an end, a contrivance used to get by, as in 'make shift'.

clue.text: Carry prophetic book, briefly, like an emblem

parts.note: to tote is to carry

indicators.note: briefly means the name of the book is shortened

parts.note: Micah is one of the books of the Old Testament prophets

explanation.surface: Someone lugs a book of prophecy around as a sort of badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts MICAH to MIC, the standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem of a clan, so totemic is relating to or like such an emblem.

clue.text: Castaway genius worked out coastal geological formation

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A clever castaway figured out the rocks along the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' rearranges CASTAWAY GENIUS. The Giant's Causeway is in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Giant's Causeway is a famous coastal formation of basalt columns in County Antrim, Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Relaxed about second girl getting cards?

indicators.note: getting means taking in, so the turned word holds the other pieces
about here means turned around, so the word for relaxed is read backwards

parts.note: laid back means relaxed, so laid
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A laid-back man is relaxed about a second girlfriend getting cards.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, 'getting your cards' means being sacked, so 'cards?' stands for the sacking.
explanation.definitionFit: In British idiom, being given your cards means being sacked, so cards stands for the sacking itself.

clue.text: In the gallery winged cherubs strike one

parts.note: to putt is to strike a golf ball gently
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: In an art gallery, a visitor lashes out at a painting of cherubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' is the gentle golf stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are the chubby winged child-figures, like cherubs, found in Renaissance paintings in galleries.

clue.text: Lines about receding river abounding with grasses

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the lines enclose the river

parts.note: RY, short for railway, means lines

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the river's name runs backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Lines of reeds and grasses grow beside a river as it goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' makes the river run backwards; the Dee flows through Wales, Chester and Aberdeen.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall grasses, so a place thick with them is reedy.

clue.text: He delivers ammunition to crew

parts.note: rounds are units of ammunition
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: Someone hands ammunition to a gun crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundsman is a tradesman, such as a milkman, who delivers along a regular round.

clue.text: Go nearly mad throughout a period of revolution

indicators.note: mad suggests letters in a wild, crazy jumble

explanation.surface: Someone almost goes crazy during a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges GO NEARLY. 'revolution' is not political: a year is one revolution of the earth round the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is one revolution of the earth round the sun, so lasting a full one is lasting a year.

clue.text: Maze reached by rail, travelling north minute.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Maze reached by rail, travelling north minute.': 'by rail, travelling' gives LABYRI and 'north' NTH, but 'minute' is left over with no job; the scan is blank and searches found no other version.
annotationWithheld.clue: Maze reached by rail, travelling north minute.

clue.text: Avoids directly answering criminals

definitions.meaning: to sidestep or parry a question, as in swordplay
receivers of stolen goods, who are criminals

explanation.definitionFit: A fence receives stolen goods, and to fence is to parry questions evasively.

clue.text: They bore lawyer looking into rowdy punch-ups

indicators.note: looking into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: brawls are rowdy fights
DA, District Attorney, is an American lawyer

explanation.surface: Tedious lawyers investigate drunken fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' means drill holes, not be tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small tool for boring holes in wood, so these tools bore.

clue.text: Ineffectual female left community out East

indicators.note: out means the letter for East is taken out of the community

parts.note: an abbey houses a religious community

explanation.surface: A weak woman left a community out in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes E from ABBEY, leaving ABBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby means lacking firmness or force, so feeble and ineffectual.

clue.text: Performer's way to get into Shaw

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is performer

indicators.note: to get into means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Artie Shaw was an American bandleader and clarinettist
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: A performer finds a way to break into a George Bernard Shaw play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaw' looks like the playwright George Bernard Shaw; it is the American bandleader.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Canons run it in church, rejecting display

indicators.note: in places the first pieces within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: rejecting means thrown back, so the word for display runs backwards

parts.note: to air is to display

explanation.surface: Church rules are kept in a church that turns down showiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canons' are rules, not clergy or guns, though the church in the clue pulls toward clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Canons are principles or standards by which things are judged.

clue.text: The remainder dwell permanently outside university

indicators.note: outside means the first piece is put around the other

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere permanently

explanation.surface: The rest of them live permanently away from the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts RESIDE around U.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains after the rest has been removed.

clue.text: Sound of punt makes us jump for joy

indicators.note: sound of signals a word heard, not seen, with a different spelling

parts.note: to punt is to bet, to gamble

explanation.surface: A bet that comes off makes us leap with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of' turns GAMBLE into GAMBOL. 'punt' is not the boat: it is the bet.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to skip or leap about playfully, as in joy.

clue.text: Mix in chopped rind later

indicators.note: chopped suggests the letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe says to mix in chopped rind later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' rearranges RIND LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlard is to intersperse or mix something in throughout, originally with fat.

clue.text: First principle when taken in for a second time

indicators.note: taken in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used for a repeat
as can mean when

explanation.surface: A first principle is absorbed only on a second hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bis is the musical direction for 'repeat', literally 'twice'.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the foundation or underlying principle of something.

clue.text: Shrub Remus's brother found, touring island

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the first piece circles the other

parts.note: in the Uncle Remus stories animals are called Brer, meaning brother

explanation.surface: Romulus finds a bush while travelling round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remus's brother' wants to be Romulus; it is Brer, the word for brother in Uncle Remus stories. 'touring' puts BRER round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A brier is a prickly shrub such as the wild rose or bramble.

clue.text: Former nurse with quarters in German city

parts.note: E and S are two compass quarters, east and south
SEN, State Enrolled Nurse, was a former UK nursing grade

explanation.surface: A retired nurse has rooms in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: SEN (State Enrolled Nurse) was a British nursing grade now discontinued.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, Germany.

clue.text: Through which we see dog hiding in centre of lodge

indicators.note: hiding means the first piece conceals the others inside it

parts.note: bow-wow is a childish word for a dog

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the word lodge

explanation.surface: A dog lurks in the middle of a hunting lodge, watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Through which we see' is a cryptic definition of a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow window is a curved bay window, something we look out through.

clue.text: In which operators have limited access

definitions.text: In which operators have limited access

parts.words: In which operators have limited access
parts.note: operators sound like telephonists, but here they are surgeons working through a tiny opening

explanation.definitionFit: Keyhole surgery is done through very small incisions, so surgeons have only narrow access to the body.
